name: Refugee Status Determination (Refugio)

qualifying_event.description: Any person in Ecuador fearing persecution in their home country may apply for refugee status determination, entirely online via the gob.ec portal ('Determinación de la condición de refugiado o apátrida'). No supporting documents are required to start the claim, though applicants may submit them if available. A renewable 6-month humanitarian visa is issued after the interview while the claim is pending.
qualifying_event.evidence_hint: Online application via gob.ec with personal information and email verification; supporting persecution evidence where available (not mandatory to file).

requirements.blocker_text: Must meet the refugee or stateless-person definition; application should be submitted as soon as possible after entering the country, though no fixed deadline is stated.

evidence_required.document: Online application (gob.ec, no supporting documents mandatory to file)

outcome.duration_length: If approved: international protection visa, valid 2 years as temporary residence. While pending: renewable 6-month humanitarian visa issued after interview.

sources.title: UNHCR Ecuador help site, republishing the official gob.ec application procedure -- fully online claim process, no mandatory documents to file, 6-month renewable humanitarian visa pending decision, 2-year international protection visa on approval

notes: NEW COUNTRY BUILD (Ecuador). work_rights modeled 'restricted' for the pending-decision humanitarian-visa period since the source did not confirm unrestricted work rights at that stage; citizenship_after_months (24) uses ec_naturalisation.json's reduced 2-year refugee/stateless naturalisation track rather than the standard 3-year track. No processing-time figure is stated by the source beyond 'may take time... due to high application volume' -- not modeled as a numeric selection_odds or timeframe to avoid inventing a figure. Ecuador has historically hosted one of the largest refugee populations in Latin America (predominantly Colombian and more recently Venezuelan) -- source tier for this file's sole citation counted as tier-1 since it verbatim republishes the official gob.ec procedure, though it is hosted on a UNHCR (tier-2 organization) domain rather than gob.ec directly.
